focus: Exodus 37 records Bezalel making the furnishings for the tent according to the pattern given in Exodus 25 and 30: the ark and mercy seat, the table, the lampstand, and the incense altar. The chapter closes with the holy anointing oil and pure incense, completing the furnishings and supplies made here, while the tabernacle itself is set up in Exodus 40.

sections.title: Bezalel Makes the Ark and the Mercy Seat
sections.summary: Bezalel makes the ark of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, with rings and poles for carrying it. He makes the mercy seat of pure gold with two cherubim of one piece with it, their wings spread above and their faces toward the mercy seat.

sections.title: The Table and Its Utensils
sections.summary: Bezalel makes the table of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with a frame, rings, and poles. He makes its dishes, cups, bowls, and pitchers of pure gold.

sections.title: The Golden Lampstand
sections.summary: The lampstand is made of one hammered piece of pure gold, with six branches and bowls like almond blossoms. Bezalel makes its seven lamps, wick-trimmers, and trays from a talent of pure gold.

sections.title: The Incense Altar, Anointing Oil, and Incense
sections.summary: Bezalel makes the square incense altar of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with its horns, molding, rings, and poles. He also makes “the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices” (Exodus 37:29).

1.brief: Bezalel makes the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide and high. The chief craftsman personally makes the holiest furnishing.
1.explain:
“Then Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood;”

“Bezalel” himself makes the ark. The chief craftsman personally makes the holiest furnishing.

“two and a half cubits was its length, a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.”

The measurements match God’s instructions in 25:10.
1.notes: Exodus 37:1–29 records the making of the furnishings described in 25:10–40 and 30:1–10, 22–38. The explanations given there apply here. The chapter shows the pattern becoming usable furnishings.

2.brief: Bezalel overlays the ark with pure gold inside and out and makes a gold molding around it. The ark is made as God described.
2.explain:
“He overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a molding of gold all around it.”

The ark is overlaid with gold and given a gold molding (25:11).

3.brief: Bezalel casts four gold rings for its corners, two on each side. The ark is prepared for carrying.
3.explain:
“And he cast for it four rings of gold to be set in its four corners: two rings on one side, and two rings on the other side of it.”

The four rings are set at the ark’s four corners, two on each side, so that poles can pass through them and the ark can be carried by them (25:12–14).

4.brief: Bezalel makes poles of acacia wood and overlays them with gold. The carrying poles are finished.
4.explain:
“He made poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.”

The carrying poles are made (25:13).

5.brief: Bezalel puts the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it. The ark is ready to travel with Israel.
5.explain:
“And he put the poles into the rings at the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.”

The ark is ready to travel with Israel (25:14).

6.brief: Bezalel makes the mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. The place of meeting is made.
6.explain:
“He also made the mercy seat of pure gold;”

“The mercy seat” is made of solid gold. This is the place where God promised to meet with Moses (25:22).

“two and a half cubits was its length and a cubit and a half its width.”

Its size matches the ark (25:17).

7.brief: Bezalel makes two cherubim of beaten gold of one piece at the two ends of the mercy seat. The cherubim are formed with the mercy seat.
7.explain:
“He made two cherubim of beaten gold;”

The “cherubim” are hammered from gold (25:18).

“he made them of one piece at the two ends of the mercy seat:”

They are formed “of one piece” with the mercy seat.

8.brief: One cherub is at each end, of one piece with the mercy seat. The design follows God’s instructions exactly.
8.explain:
“one cherub at one end on this side, and the other cherub at the other end on that side. He made the cherubim at the two ends of one piece with the mercy seat.”

One cherub stands at each end (25:19). The design follows God’s instructions exactly.

9.brief: The cherubim spread their wings above, cover the mercy seat, and face one another toward it. The finished mercy seat matches the pattern of Exodus 25.
9.explain:
“The cherubim spread out their wings above, and covered the mercy seat with their wings.”

Their wings spread over the mercy seat (25:20).

“They faced one another; the faces of the cherubim were toward the mercy seat.”

They face the mercy seat. The finished work matches the pattern. The mercy seat keeps its distinct role as the place of meeting and atonement, which Hebrews connects with Christ’s priestly work (Hebrews 9:5, 11–14).

10.brief: Bezalel makes the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high. The table for the showbread is made.
10.explain:
“He made the table of acacia wood; two cubits was its length, a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.”

The table for the showbread is made (25:23).

11.brief: Bezalel overlays the table with pure gold and makes a gold molding around it. The table is fitted for God’s presence.
11.explain:
“And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made a molding of gold all around it.”

The table is overlaid with gold (25:24).

12.brief: Bezalel makes a frame a handbreadth wide around it with a gold molding. The details are completed.
12.explain:
“Also he made a frame of a handbreadth all around it, and made a molding of gold for the frame all around it.”

The frame and molding are added (25:25).

13.brief: Bezalel casts four gold rings for the corners at its legs. The table is prepared for carrying.
13.explain:
“And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners that were at its four legs.”

The table is prepared for carrying (25:26).

14.brief: The rings are close to the frame as holders for the poles. The table can travel with the sanctuary.
14.explain:
“The rings were close to the frame, as holders for the poles to bear the table.”

The rings hold the poles (25:27).

15.brief: Bezalel makes the poles of acacia wood overlaid with gold. The table’s carrying poles are finished.
15.explain:
“And he made the poles of acacia wood to bear the table, and overlaid them with gold.”

The carrying poles are finished (25:28).

16.brief: Bezalel makes the table’s dishes, cups, bowls, and pitchers of pure gold. The utensils for its service are completed.
16.explain:
“He made of pure gold the utensils which were on the table: its dishes, its cups, its bowls, and its pitchers for pouring.”

The utensils for the table are made of gold (25:29). The table provides for bread before the LORD, a picture of Christ, who nourishes His people (John 6:35). The table keeps its own function, distinct from the mercy seat.

17.brief: Bezalel makes the lampstand of pure hammered gold, its shaft, branches, bowls, knobs, and flowers all of one piece. The lampstand is made as a single work.
17.explain:
“He also made the lampstand of pure gold; of hammered work he made the lampstand.”

The “lampstand” is hammered from pure gold (25:31).

“Its shaft, its branches, its bowls, its ornamental knobs, and its flowers were of the same piece.”

It is made “of the same piece,” a single work.

18.brief: Six branches come out of its sides, three on each side. The branches spread its light.
18.explain:
“And six branches came out of its sides: three branches of the lampstand out of one side, and three branches of the lampstand out of the other side.”

Six branches spread its light (25:32).

19.brief: Each branch has three almond-blossom bowls with a knob and a flower. The lampstand is shaped like a flowering tree.
19.explain:
“There were three bowls made like almond blossoms on one branch, with an ornamental knob and a flower,”

Each branch carries three cups shaped like almond blossoms. Each cup has an ornamental knob, a rounded bud-like swelling, and a flower, an opened bloom (25:33).

“and three bowls made like almond blossoms on the other branch, with an ornamental knob and a flower—and so for the six branches coming out of the lampstand.”

The same pattern repeats on all six branches, so the lampstand looks like a flowering almond tree.

20.brief: The central shaft has four almond-blossom bowls with their knobs and flowers. The main stem is richly formed.
20.explain:
“And on the lampstand itself were four bowls made like almond blossoms, each with its ornamental knob and flower.”

The central shaft has four of these almond-blossom cups, one more than each branch (25:34).

21.brief: A knob is placed under each pair of branches. The branches are joined to the shaft.
21.explain:
“There was a knob under the first two branches of the same, a knob under the second two branches of the same, and a knob under the third two branches of the same, according to the six branches extending from it.”

The six branches come out in three pairs, one branch on each side at each of three levels. Under each pair, where it leaves the shaft, sits a knob. The three knobs mark the three places where the branches join the shaft (25:35).

22.brief: The knobs and branches are of one piece, all one hammered piece of pure gold. The lampstand is a unified whole.
22.explain:
“Their knobs and their branches were of one piece; all of it was one hammered piece of pure gold.”

The knobs, the branches, and the shaft were not made separately and attached. All of it was hammered from a single piece of pure gold (25:36), so the lampstand is one unified whole.

23.brief: Bezalel makes its seven lamps, wick-trimmers, and trays of pure gold. The lampstand is ready to give light.
23.explain:
“And he made its seven lamps, its wick-trimmers, and its trays of pure gold.”

The lamps and their tools are made of gold (25:37–38). The lampstand is ready to give light.

24.brief: Bezalel makes the lampstand and its utensils from a talent of pure gold. The costly lampstand is completed.
24.explain:
“Of a talent of pure gold he made it, with all its utensils.”

The lampstand used “a talent of pure gold” (25:39). Its light points to Jesus, the light of the world (John 8:12).

25.brief: Bezalel makes the incense altar of acacia wood, a cubit square and two cubits high, with horns of one piece with it. The altar of incense is made.
25.explain:
“He made the incense altar of acacia wood. Its length was a cubit and its width a cubit—it was square—and two cubits was its height.”

The “incense altar” is made (30:1–2).

“Its horns were of one piece with it.”

Its horns are part of it.

26.brief: Bezalel overlays its top, sides, and horns with pure gold and makes a gold molding around it. The incense altar matches the gold of the holy place.
26.explain:
“And he overlaid it with pure gold: its top, its sides all around, and its horns.”

It is overlaid with gold (30:3).

“He also made for it a molding of gold all around it.”

The incense altar matches the gold of the holy place.

27.brief: Bezalel makes two gold rings under its molding to hold the poles. The altar is prepared for carrying.
27.explain:
“He made two rings of gold for it under its molding, by its two corners on both sides, as holders for the poles with which to bear it.”

The altar is prepared for carrying (30:4).

28.brief: Bezalel makes the poles of acacia wood and overlays them with gold. The incense altar is finished.
28.explain:
“And he made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.”

The incense altar is finished (30:5). It will serve the worship appointed in 30:7–10, a picture of prayer and Christ’s intercession (Revelation 5:8; Hebrews 7:25).

29.brief: Bezalel also makes “the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices,” according to the perfumer’s art. The oil and incense complete the items made in this chapter, ready for the sanctuary’s service.
29.explain:
“He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, according to the work of the perfumer.”

Bezalel also prepares “the holy anointing oil” and “the pure incense” according to God’s recipes (30:22–38). These complete the items made in this chapter, ready for the sanctuary’s service.
